subject: Sandboxed data rights, no-training proof, and subprocessor evidence request
messages:
From: Sylvia Jones <sylvia.jones@medsync.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: model-improvement opt-out + residency for POC

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the latency numbers look promising for our telehealth workflows. Before we proceed with the POC contract, legal asked for a short list of guarantees and evidence around three things:

1) No-training / model improvement opt-out: we need a contractual "no-training" commitment for any PII or clinical prompts sent during the POC and a short list of artifacts you can provide to show you won't feed data into model training pipelines.
2) Prompt/response ownership and exportability: our product team will want proof that transcripts and generated responses are exportable on demand and that we retain ownership of our customers' prompts/outputs.
3) Subprocessor residency & transfers: can you confirm which subprocessors may touch our data for the hosted option and if any transfers to EU/APAC occur?

I've attached our internal privacy requirements (MedSync_privacy_requirements.docx) for reference. Can you share what evidence you can provide and whether a Dedicated or Private deployment is needed to meet these asks?

Appreciate a short bullet list we can hand to procurement.

Best,
Sylvia
Sylvia Jones
Head of Compliance, MedSync

(attachment: medsync_privacy_requirements.docx)

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Jones <sylvia.jones@medsync.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: model-improvement opt-out + residency for POC

Hi Sylvia — thanks for the write-up and the doc. Short answer up-front: yes, we can contractually commit to a no-training/no-model-improvement clause for POC data and provide multiple forms of evidence. Below are concise bullets you can pass to procurement/legal.

- No-training commitment: we can include a DPA addendum that prohibits using MedSync POC data for model training or improvement (no derivation to base models or fine-tuning).
- Evidence types we can deliver during/after POC:
  * Subprocessor inventory CSV snapshot (signed/immutable export)
  * Audit log extract showing request/response IDs and storage operations
  * Short ops attestation (SRE) describing retention policies and retention timeframe for POC data
  * Demonstration of export path (SFTP / API export) with sample transcript (metadata-only)
- Ownership: contract language can explicitly state MedSync retains IP/ownership of prompts and outputs generated from your inputs during the POC.
- Deployment recommendation: for strongest residency guarantees and fewer subprocessors, Dedicated or Private deployment is preferred; hosted API is possible with scoping.

I'm attaching a short internal checklist we use to collect the above evidence for customers. If you like, Marissa (legal) and Dev (ops) are on copy to scope what's feasible for a 4-week POC.

Next steps: 1) confirm which evidence items MedSync needs first, 2) schedule a 30-min call to walk procurement through artifacts.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
(attachment: no_train_evidence_checklist.pdf)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Jones <sylvia.jones@medsync.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Q: model-improvement opt-out + residency for POC

Hi Sylvia — looping in a couple of legal points to make procurement's review faster. High-level legal options we typically offer for POCs:

1) DPA Addendum + No-Training Rider (simple): a short addendum that states we will not use any MedSync POC data to train or improve models. We include explicit examples (prompts, logs, embeddings).
2) Technical Controls Schedule (ops): lists the evidence artifacts Redwood will deliver and the cadence (end-of-POC export + on-request audit log extract).
3) Subprocessor restrictions: we can commit to a limited subprocessor set for the POC (list), and we can provide a one-time snapshot of subcontractors with IP addresses and regions.

A couple of redlines you should expect from large healthcare customers: exportability language (how outputs are returned), retention window (we typically support configurable retention for Dedicated/Private), and a proof-of-flow exhibit that shows the data path (ingest -> ephemeral KV cache -> short-term storage -> export).

I'll draft suggested clause language (short, plain English) and a Technical Controls Schedule for the POC. Dev, can you confirm which artifacts we can generate within two business days for a POC start?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks — a few clarifying Qs from procurement/legal side:

1) If we use the hosted API for the POC, which subprocessors will see request/response payloads? Please be explicit (names + regions).
2) Will audit logs include full request/response content or only metadata IDs? We need a way to map transcripts back to customer IDs for incident response.
3) Regarding KV/prefix caching: can you provide a design note that confirms cached KV is ephemeral and excluded from training pipelines?

If you can share the Technical Controls Schedule and a subprocessor snapshot this week, we can move the SOW sign-off next week.

Tom Alvarez

Subject: Re: Quick Q: model-improvement opt-out + residency for POC

Tom — answers inline and attached a short ops note. Highlights:

- Subprocessors (hosted API): current list available at https://redwood.app/subprocessors.csv. For hosted POC the common subprocessors that may process payloads: FastStorage Co. (US), EdgeCache LLC (US), and MetricsLoggers Ltd. (Ireland) for metrics/observability. For Dedicated we can limit to a smaller footprint (no MetricsLoggers).
- Audit logs: we can provide a log extract that contains request IDs, timestamps, requester identity, and full request/response payloads for the POC period on an as-requested basis (encrypted export). We typically redact third-party system internals but will provide mapping metadata to link transcripts to customer IDs.
- KV/prefix caching: design note confirms KV is ephemeral (TTL default 30 minutes for POC) and cache contents are not used for model training. Permanent stores used for analytics are logically separated and require explicit retention policies in the Technical Controls Schedule.

Attached: ops_design_kv_no_train.txt (short note) and an exportable subprocessor CSV snapshot.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa will share a suggested DPA addendum and Technical Controls Schedule by EOD.
2) We’ll provide the subprocessor snapshot and an audit-log extract sample within 48 hours.
3) Schedule a 30-min call (calendar link below) to walk procurement through artifact formats.

Calendar: https://cal.com/kimberly/medsync-privacy-call

Thanks,
Kimberly
(attachments: ops_design_kv_no_train.txt, subprocessors_snapshot_20260914.csv)
